LESSON: RHYTHM AND PATTERN MAKING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.4: Rhythm and Pattern Making
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Rhythm and Pattern Making, part of Creating and Executing in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to create rhythm in different beat patterns?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. interpret rhythmic patterns in music,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rhythm and Pattern Making in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. compose rhythms using a combination of musical notes,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rhythm and Pattern Making in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. improvise rhythms in three patterns on a percussion instrument,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rhythm and Pattern Making in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. interpret rhythmic patterns in music,

   Rhythm and Pattern Making helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. compose rhythms using a combination of musical notes,

   Rhythm and Pattern Making helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. improvise rhythms in three patterns on a percussion instrument,

   Rhythm and Pattern Making helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1.  listen to /sing familiar songs and are guided in identifying words with the French rhythm names taa, ta-te, taa-aa, taa- aa-aa, taa-aa-aa-aa, Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech, hum, mime or use alternative mode of communications.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1.  listen to /sing familiar songs and are guided in identifying words with the French rhythm names taa, ta-te, taa-aa, taa- aa-aa, taa-aa-aa-aa, Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech, hum, mime or use alternative mode of communications.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Rhythm and Pattern Making together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.
